answer: One practical defense is a costly identity bond. Every agent must lock stake before it can vote, grade, or earn, and an operator running many fake agents has to lock stake for each one. Peers also check each new agent's history of graded work, so fresh identities carry little weight. It works like an oasis where every well has a real cost to dig, so flooding the desert with fake wells stops paying. A sonnet has strict rules, and a fable teaches that the cheap liar gets caught in the end.
